name: Colombia
headline: Colombia: +2.6% growth in 2025, 5.1% inflation, debt 60% of GDP
sections: Colombia is a $457 billion economy (2025), the world's 38th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +2.6% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $23K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 9.9% of GDP (2025).
Consumer prices rose 5.1% in 2025, above typical targets, down from 10.2% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 8.0% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 17.7% (2025).
Gross government debt is 60% of GDP (2025), a moderate level that has fallen from 65% in 2020. The general government balance is −5.8% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is −2.4% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 35% of GDP (2025), a relatively closed economy. Net FDI inflows were 2.5% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 65% of GDP by 2031, still rising from today's level. Life expectancy is 77.9 years (2024). Population: 53.0 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
